question: THE 3-Z^2 SEQUENCE TEST -- the mechanistic hook's next member, pre-registered: does the SAME 3 Z^2-class structure (100.531 = 100 - 0.53%, A01) appear at ANY OTHER SM mass scale?  The family m_i/100.531^n (n = 0,1,2) vs the framework's keV-scale ladder (the 5.09-keV m band, the cluster 334-K energy 2.88e-5 keV, the 9.17-K phase energy 7.91e-7 keV), the expected FDR stated BEFORE the fit, the survivors, and the honest verdict -- sequence member found or sequence closed.

family.formula: m_i / (3 Z^2)^n, n in {0,1,2}, i in {e,mu,tau,p,n} (15 members)

ladder_registers.L0_m_band_5p09keV: the committed m band (G212 peak 5.0886; band [4.9917, 5.1855]; canonical cosmic-noon 5.051 keV)
ladder_registers.L1_cluster_334K: the cluster 334-K-class energy = k_B x 334 K (Z07 measured T_dark(2-5 R500))
ladder_registers.L2_phase_9p17K: the 9.17-K phase energy = k_B x 9.1744 K (G151 T_phase at the triad sigma)

pre_registration.state: EXPECTED <N> = 0.10 coincidences in the pre-registered family at the 1% tolerance, stated BEFORE the run

gate.explanation: any survivor sits inside the +-10% band of its own rung -> its E_chance >= 0.10 = 300x above E* = 3.29e-4

verdicts.V1: THE PRE-REGISTERED FAMILY TABLE: the 5 SM masses x n = {0,1,2} = 15 members (m_i/100.531^n) vs the 3-rung ladder at the 1% tolerance.  15 x 3 = 45 comparisons, expected count <N> = 0.10 (the null's window math: only m_e/100.531 = 5.0830 keV sits within +-10% of the 5.09-keV rung; L1 (334 K = 2.878e-5 keV) and L2 (9.17 K = 7.906e-7 keV) have ZERO members within +-10%, the family's smallest member m_e/100.531^2 = 0.0506 keV being 1756x above L1).  One survivor: m_e/100.531 vs L0 at 0.11% -- the A01 hook itself.  No other member comes within 1% of ANY rung (next closest: m_mu/100.531^2 = 10.45 keV at 2.05x L0; everything else >= 18x).
verdicts.V2: THE SURVIVORS: exactly ONE member survives at the 1% tolerance -- m_e/100.531 = 5.083 keV vs the committed m band rung 5.0886 keV, delta -0.11%, z = -0.058 sigma vs G212 (inside the 1-sigma band [4.992, 5.186]).  This is the PRE-EXISTING A01 hook that DEFINED the family -- its survival is by construction, not evidence.  ADDITIONAL survivors at other SM scales: 0.  The same 3-Z^2-class structure appears at NO other SM mass scale.
verdicts.V3: THE HONEST STATEMENT -- THE NUMBER THAT TELLS: the 3-Z^2 sequence is CLOSED.  Pre-registered expectation <N> = 0.10 coincidences in the 15-member family at the 1% tolerance; the run finds the expected single member (m_e/100.531 = 5.083 keV vs the 5.09-keV ladder, the A01 hook) and ZERO additional members: m_mu/100.531-class (1050.8, 10.45 keV), m_p/100.531-class (9333, 92.84 keV), m_n/100.531-class (9346, 92.97 keV), m_tau/100.531-class (17675, 175.8 keV), m_e/100.531^2 (50.6 eV) all miss every ladder rung by >= 100% (most by >= 10x).  The gate is closed twice over: (i) FDR - the hook's own chance rate is E_chance = 0.10 = 300x ABOVE the family-wise E* = 3.3e-4 (THRESHOLD.py), and pre-registered as impassable for the family (any survivor carries its own +-10% presence); (ii) MECHANISM - the only framework reading on record (100 = 3 Z^2 - 0.53%) is the m_e hook itself and generalizes to NO other scale, so no next member exists to carry it.  FINAL REGISTER: m_e/100 is a SINGLE COINCIDENCE (the A01 hook at z = +0.22 sigma against G212, with the 3-Z^2 hook at 0.53% post-hoc); the sequence test CLOSES the question - the mechanistic hook has no next member.

final_register.hook_status: m_e/100 is a SINGLE COINCIDENCE (A01: pre-existing pair at z = +0.22 sigma vs G212; 3 Z^2 hook at 0.53%, post-hoc, 3.3-3.75 bits < 10-bit gate)

gates.a_pre_registered: PASS -- the family (5 SM masses x n = 0,1,2 = 15 members), the tolerance (1%), the ladder (5.09 keV / 334 K / 9.17 K) and the expected count (<N> = 0.10 from the null's window math) are all stated BEFORE the survival scan runs, and the scan is a deterministic lookup over the declared family.
gates.b_fdr: PASS -- the null's own window math (gate/fdr.py _poisson_e_chance) prices the family: E_chance = 0.10 for the 5.09-keV rung (the hook alone in the +-10% band), 0 for the 334-K and 9.17-K rungs, <N> = 0.10 total.  The ONE found coincidence (the hook) is the expected member, not a surplus; a second would have been ~10x the null.  Family-wise E* = 3.29e-4 is impassable by construction (any survivor's E_chance >= 0.10).
gates.c_accuracy: PASS (bridge level as registered) -- the hook sits at 0.11% from the m band (inside its 1-sigma width +-1.9%); the sequence claim is structural (member present/absent at 1%), not kepler-grade.
gates.d_mechanism: FAIL for any next member -- the only mechanism on record (100 = 3 Z^2 - 0.53%) is the m_e hook itself; m_mu, m_p, m_n, m_tau at 100.531^n land 100%-2000% from every ladder rung, so no member exists to carry it.  The m_e/100 hook stands alone: SINGLE COINCIDENCE, sequence closed.
gates.e_framework_origin: PASS -- every input is committed framework/SM: 3 and Z (null germs), the 5 SM masses (CODATA/PDG pdg_constants), the ladder rungs (G212, Z07, G151), the E* (THRESHOLD.py); nothing refit.
gates.f_falsifier: REGISTERED -- (i) any measured SM-scale mass m_i and keV-ladder energy E with |m_i/100.531^n - E|/E <= 1% for n in {1,2}, i != e re-OPENS the sequence (a gate-clearing member needs E_chance < 3.3e-4 AND a mechanism); (ii) |m_meas - m_e/100| > 1% kills the pair (A01's standing falsifier); (iii) a measured m_e/100.531-class relic mass at any OTHER scale is the sequence's discovery channel.
